title: Hotline frames-v1 payload and mailbox-v1 transport contract
description: The shared wire contract for frames-v1 JSON text payloads and the additive mailbox-v1 transport controls that carry them. Mailbox controls are routed outside the transcript reducer; payload remains verbatim frames-v1 text.
$comment: Mailbox-v1 is frozen here for independent relay, box, and mobile implementations. Implementations remain hand-written and must conform to this schema and its protocol fixtures.

mailboxCursor.description: Canonical non-negative base-10 mailbox cursor M. It is always a JSON string, including above 2^53; implementations compare it with BigInt or decimal-safe comparison and never Number(M) or parseInt(M).

mailboxId.description: Opaque public mailbox routing identifier. It names exactly one bot/device mailbox and is never a wildcard, list, or broadcast selector.

mailboxGrant.description: Per-bot/device grant issued once after box pairing, then stored durably and reused. It carries at least 128 bits of entropy, is hash-verified on every mailbox_sync, and remains valid until revoked.

envelopeId.description: Opaque addressed-envelope identifier. For every journal-backed durable dispatch it is deterministic f(journal_seq, device_id), created inside the atomic journal-plus-dispatch write and never at send or retry time; retrying that recipient event therefore reuses it and unique (mailbox_id, envelope_id) insertion is idempotent. A non-journal ephemeral signal instead uses a sender-stable identifier because it has no J or dispatch row.

plainV1Encoding.description: TLS-only mailbox migration encoding for unchanged frames-v1 JSON text.

plainV1Payload.description: Opaque, verbatim frames-v1 JSON text. The relay stores and forwards these bytes as text without parsing, reducing, or rewriting the inner frame.

device_payload.title: Relay and box: virtual device payload
device_payload.description: Carries one verbatim frames-v1 payload on the virtual device stream. Exactly one routing key is present: connection_id during bootstrap or mailbox_id after provisioning. On relay-to-box traffic, device_id is trusted only when supplied from the relay's connection/grant binding; client-supplied identity inside payload is ignored.

device_id.description: Relay-bound device metadata for relay-to-box traffic. This field is authoritative only after relay binding; an identically named client payload field never binds identity.

mailbox_provision.title: Box to relay: provision mailbox
mailbox_provision.description: Binds a relay-assigned bootstrap connection to the device identity authenticated by the box after pairing succeeds. Client-supplied device fields are not an identity source.

mailbox_provisioned.title: Relay to box and device: mailbox provisioned
mailbox_provisioned.description: Returns the one-device mailbox route, current head, and newly issued durable grant to the box and bootstrap connection. The grant is issued once, not usable once.

device_id.description: Device identity authenticated by the box during provisioning.

device_send.title: Device to relay: send virtual device payload
device_send.description: Queues one source-addressed device payload for the box. Its sender-stable envelope_id deduplicates offline copies; after forwarding, the box's durable inner CID result handles retries. This pre-journal identifier is distinct from the deterministic box-dispatch envelopeId definition.

mailbox_enqueue.title: Box to relay: enqueue addressed envelope
mailbox_enqueue.description: Offers one envelope to exactly one mailbox. Durable offers are inserted idempotently by (mailbox_id, envelope_id); ephemeral offers become signals and receive no M.

expires_at.description: Envelope expiry timestamp; relay durable retention is capped at seven days.

mailbox_enqueued.title: Relay to box: durable envelope accepted
mailbox_enqueued.description: Reports durable dispatch acceptance, not chat receipt. A duplicate returns the original mailbox_seq and state without creating another push intent.

mailbox_sync.title: Device to relay: synchronize mailbox
mailbox_sync.description: First frame on a mailbox socket. Authenticates the durable grant and requests a bounded page strictly after the supplied mailbox cursor.

limit.description: Positive requested page size, bounded by the relay.

mailbox_state.title: Relay to device: mailbox state
mailbox_state.description: Opens a sync snapshot with its retained floor and captured head. reset_required couples mailbox reset to journal recovery and clearing the local mailbox cursor.

mailbox_item.title: Relay to device: durable mailbox item
mailbox_item.description: Carries one durable addressed envelope and M. The client commits envelope/event dedup, its frames-v1 projection, J, and M before cumulatively acknowledging M.

mailbox_signal.title: Relay to device: ephemeral mailbox signal
mailbox_signal.description: Carries one addressed ephemeral envelope. It has no mailbox_seq, durable storage, push intent, or acknowledgement.

mailbox_synced.title: Relay to device: mailbox snapshot page complete
mailbox_synced.description: Ends one snapshot page. Live mailbox_item delivery starts only after the captured snapshot is fully flushed; envelope dedup spans that boundary.

mailbox_ack.title: Device to relay: cumulative mailbox acknowledgement
mailbox_ack.description: Cumulatively acknowledges committed delivery through M for exactly one mailbox. through is never a journal cursor J.

mailbox_push_set.title: Device to relay: set mailbox push registration
mailbox_push_set.description: Registers generic relay push when enabled or unregisters it when disabled. Push carries only Hotline activity and the opaque local route.

token.description: Expo push token, required when enabled is true.

route.description: Opaque local route, required when enabled is true.

mailbox_revoke.title: Box to relay: revoke mailbox
mailbox_revoke.description: Revokes one mailbox's grant and push token and closes its bound socket. It has no wildcard form.

mailbox_error.title: Relay mailbox transport error
mailbox_error.description: Mailbox-layer failure routed before frames-v1 payload parsing. It is not the frames-v1 error payload shape and never reaches parseFrame, the reducer, or the transcript. mailbox_full alone retries unchanged; mailbox_gap invokes journal recovery; other codes require credential or state repair.

relayPresence.title: Relay to server: device presence
relayPresence.description: A relay-owned, bot-inbound control carrying the current count of open device sockets. It is consumed only on the dialed relay transport and is never journaled or sent to app clients.

devices.description: Current count of open device WebSockets at the relay.

relayBlobRef.title: Relay blob capability reference
relayBlobRef.description: A relative capability reference returned by the configured relay. Implementations derive the origin from local configuration and never trust this object as a request origin.

key.description: A 24-byte random capability encoded as 32 unpadded base64url characters.

expires_at.description: Logical blob expiry as an RFC3339 timestamp.

fileRef.title: Attachment file reference
fileRef.description: An attachment descriptor with a local authenticated URL and, when relay-backed, an additive relay blob capability for the same bytes.

size.description: File size in bytes, when known.

url.description: Authenticated attachment URL, normally relative to the app-channel server.

blob.description: Relay fetch capability for the same bytes; additive to the local /att/ URL.

artifactRef.title: Static HTML artifact reference
artifactRef.description: One self-contained HTML artifact rendered under the static-html-v1 sandbox policy.

clientToServerHello.title: App to server: hello
clientToServerHello.description: The first frame on a connection. It declares v1, authenticates the device, names it, and supplies its replay cursor.

last_seq.description: Highest server sequence already seen by this client.

capabilities.description: Optional mailbox capability offer. Legacy clients omit it; old servers ignore it as an unknown field.

clientToServerSend.title: App to server: send
clientToServerSend.description: A typed user message, optionally replying to an existing message.

id.description: Stored attachment identifier (content-addressed name) previously returned by a deferred upload.

name.description: Optional display filename for the attachment.

mime.description: Declared photo MIME for a relay blob attachment.

size.description: Declared byte size for a relay blob attachment.

blob.description: Relay capability to materialize before sink delivery.

attachments.description: Staged attachments (up to ten) sent together as one harness turn. Direct attachments reference a prior defer=1 upload; relay photos add mime, size, and blob for box-side materialization.

cids.description: Per-attachment client identifiers, aligned by index with attachments, so each server sent echo carries the originating client's cid for optimistic-bubble adoption.

clientToServerTap.title: App to server: tap
clientToServerTap.description: A selection from a message's button row.

msg_id.description: Identifier of the message that owns the button row.

clientToServerReact.title: App to server: react
clientToServerReact.description: A user reaction to an existing message.

msg_id.description: Identifier of the message receiving the reaction.

serverToClientWelcome.title: Server to app: welcome
serverToClientWelcome.description: Accepts a hello and identifies the authenticated device, bot, and current replay cursor.

capabilities.description: Optional echo of the negotiated mailbox capability. Legacy servers omit it; old clients ignore it as an unknown field.

serverToClientPairing.title: Server to app: pairing
serverToClientPairing.description: Reports that the device is awaiting operator approval.

serverToClientError.title: Server to app: error
serverToClientError.description: Reports a protocol, authentication, pairing, or action-delivery failure.

cid.description: For delivery_failed, correlates the rejected action so it can be retried.

serverToClientAck.title: Server to app: ack
serverToClientAck.description: Acknowledges a sink-accepted inbound client frame and reports the server cursor that covers its accepted echoes.

cid.description: Client identifier copied from the acknowledged frame.

message_id.description: Turn message identifier, present only for a staged multi-photo send (the last echo's id); omitted for plain sends, taps, and reactions.

on.description: Whether the typing indicator is on.

serverToClientMsg.title: Server to app: msg
serverToClientMsg.description: One agent message bubble. Buttons, reply target, and attachment are optional.

text.description: Agent message body; empty for a file-only bubble.

buttons.description: Flat button-label list; the selected label is returned in a tap frame.

reply_to.description: Identifier of the message being answered.

serverToClientEdit.title: Server to app: edit
serverToClientEdit.description: Replaces the text of an existing message.

id.description: Identifier of the message being edited.

serverToClientReact.title: Server to app: react
serverToClientReact.description: Applies an emoji reaction to a message. Device is present on user-reaction echoes and absent on agent reactions.

msg_id.description: Identifier of the message receiving the reaction.

device.description: Originating device identifier for a user-reaction echo.

serverToClientSent.title: Server to app: sent
serverToClientSent.description: Echoes a user-originated text, button tap, or attachment into the journal and to other connected screens.

id.description: Server message identifier assigned to the user turn.

text.description: User text or button label; may be empty for an attachment.

cid.description: Originating client identifier, when one was supplied.

kind.description: Non-text turn kind. The current server emits button for button-tap echoes; absence denotes typed text or an attachment.
